title: Geometry of distinct tuples in an affine etale atlas
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be quasi-separated, meaning that its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests, and let $a:U\to X$ be a representable etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] with $U$ affine. For every integer $p\geq1$, write $F_p=U\times_X\cdots\times_XU$ with $p$ factors. Then $F_p$ is a quasi-compact separated scheme, where separated means that the absolute diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its natural comparison morphism $F_p\to U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\cdots\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}U$ is separated and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Every pairwise equality locus $\Delta_{ij}\subset F_p$ is open and closed. Consequently $W_p=F_p\setminus\bigcup_{i<j}\Delta_{ij}$ is a quasi-compact separated scheme, open and closed in $F_p$, and $W_p\to X$ is representable etale. The open subscheme notion is [def-weil-open-immersion]. For each geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $W_p(\Omega)\times_{X(\Omega)}\{\bar x\}$ is naturally the set of ordered $p$-tuples of pairwise distinct elements of $U(\Omega)\times_{X(\Omega)}\{\bar x\}$. For $p=1$ the union of equality loci is empty.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, $F_1=U$, and $P_p=U\times_S\cdots\times_SU$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], $U$ is quasi-compact. Its identity is a monomorphism, hence separated by [lem-trf-scheme-monomorphism-separated]; [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated] applied to this identity makes $U$ absolutely separated. By [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence], $a:U\to X$ is quasi-compact because $X$ is quasi-separated; this assertion does not require $X$ quasi-compact. Induct on $p\geq1$. If $F_p$ is a scheme etale over $X$, then $F_{p+1}=F_p\times_XU$ is a scheme by representability of $a$, and its projection to $F_p$ is etale and quasi-compact by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] and [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]. Composing etale maps makes $F_{p+1}\to X$ etale. If $F_p$ is quasi-compact, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-morphism-preimage-qc-open] applied to the entire open $F_p$ makes $F_{p+1}$ quasi-compact. This proves simultaneously schemeness, quasi-compactness and representable etaleness for all $p$.

source.place: Tags 0BBN (lemma-filter-quasi-compact), first proof paragraph, and 07ST (lemma-filter-quasi-compact-quasi-separated), final paragraph; quasi-compactness by base changing the quasi-compact chart.

proof.text: Let $c_p:F_p\to P_p$ be the comparison. Iterating [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] shows $P_p$ affine. The comparison $c_1$ is the identity, hence separated and locally quasi-finite by [lem-sfb-space-fibre-product-comparison] with $A=U$ and $B=Z=T=S$. For the induction, factor $c_{p+1}$ as $F_p\times_XU\xrightarrow{j_p}F_p\times_SU\xrightarrow{k_p}P_p\times_SU$. Here $j_p$ is the binary comparison for $F_p\to X$, $U\to X$, $X\to S$. Also $k_p=c_p\times_S1_U$ is the base change of $c_p$ along $P_p\times_SU\to P_p$: both its pullback description and the displayed source classify a section of $F_p$ and a section of $U$. The composite has the $p+1$ coordinate projections, so it is precisely $c_{p+1}$.

source.place: Tag 03KN (lemma-fibre-product-after-map), clause (1), iterated binary comparison; Tag 0BBN first proof paragraph.

proof.text: Assume $c_p$ separated and locally quasi-finite. By [lem-sfb-space-fibre-product-comparison], $j_p$ is separated and locally quasi-finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change], applied to the scheme map $c_p$ and base-changing scheme $P_p\times_SU$, $k_p$ is separated and locally quasi-finite. The source and target of both arrows are schemes by step 1 and ordinary scheme fibre products. By [lem-a1-scheme-lqf-composition] and [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition], their composite $c_{p+1}$ is separated and locally quasi-finite. Induction proves the comparison assertion. Since $P_p$ is affine, [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated] then makes every $F_p$ absolutely separated.

source.place: Tag 03KN (lemma-fibre-product-after-map), clause (1); Tag 0BBN first proof paragraph, absolute separation via the comparison.

proof.text: Write $R=U\times_XU=F_2$ and let $b:R\to U\times_SU$ be the comparison. The square with top $\Delta_a:U\to R$, bottom $\Delta_{U/S}:U\to U\times_SU$, left $1_U$ and right $b$ is cartesian: on any test scheme its right-hand pullback requires the two coordinates of a pair to be the same section of $U$, and hence is uniquely that section. Step 1 gives absolute separatedness of $U$, so $\Delta_{U/S}$ is a closed immersion. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], $\Delta_a$ is a closed immersion. Thus $a$ is separated, even though $X$ need not be separated. Since $a$ is etale, the first clause of [lem-sfb-space-separated-etale-diagonal-complement] says that $\Delta_a$ is also an open immersion.

source.place: Tag 0BBN (lemma-filter-quasi-compact), first proof paragraph: separatedness of U to X and its open and closed diagonal.

proof.text: For $1\leq i<j\leq p$, let $r_{ij}:F_p\to R$ retain coordinates $i,j$. Define $\Delta_{ij}=F_p\times_{R,\Delta_a}U$. The fibre-product equation says exactly that coordinates $i$ and $j$ agree. It is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. It is open as well: since $\Delta_a$ identifies $U$ with an open subscheme of $R$, this pullback is the restriction of $F_p$ to the inverse image of that open, with the restricted structure sheaf [def-weil-open-immersion]. Thus each equality locus is open and closed. The finite union of these clopen subsets is clopen, so its complement $W_p$ is clopen. It is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact], since it is closed in the quasi-compact $F_p$.

source.place: Tags 0BBN (lemma-filter-quasi-compact), first paragraph (all diagonals), and 07ST (lemma-filter-quasi-compact-quasi-separated), final paragraph (quasi-compactness).

proof.text: The open immersion $W_p\to F_p$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation](a). Its composite with the separated absolute structure map of $F_p$ is separated by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition], so $W_p$ is absolutely separated. The same open immersion is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1). Composing with the representable etale $F_p\to X$ of step 1 using [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] makes $W_p\to X$ representable etale.

source.place: Tag 0BBN (lemma-filter-quasi-compact), first paragraph: W_p is an open and closed subscheme and is etale over X.

proof.text: Evaluate the sheaf fibre product at $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. By the compatible-pairs definition of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], a section of $F_p$ above $\bar x$ is exactly a tuple $(u_1,\ldots,u_p)$ with every $a(u_i)=\bar x$. Step 5 identifies its membership in $\Delta_{ij}$ with $u_i=u_j$. A map from the one-point spectrum of the field $\Omega$ factors through the complementary open exactly when it avoids each equality locus. Consequently its section belongs to $W_p$ exactly when the entries are pairwise distinct, giving the asserted natural bijection. Restriction of sections commutes with all coordinate projections, so the description is natural. For $p=1$ there are no pairs, $W_1=F_1=U$, and this bijection is the identity on the fibre. Empty charts and fibres give empty tuple sets for every $p\geq1$, as required.
